topic: Zener Diode as a Voltage Regulator
title: How a Zener Holds Voltage Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's bicycle dynamo makes the lamp blaze when he pedals fast and fade when he slows down. A phone cannot live with a voltage like that. How do we hold a voltage steady? We start with a water tank and an overflow pipe, then meet the real part: the Zener diode, heavily doped and connected in reverse bias on purpose.

We read the Zener V-I characteristic (almost no reverse current until breakdown at V_z, then the current shoots up while the voltage stays stuck). On a live breadboard the input rises and falls while the oscilloscope shows the changing input (CH1) and a steady 9 V across the load (CH2), and the Zener soaks up the extra current. We find every current step by step: I = (V_in - V_z)/R, I_L = V_z/R_L, I_z = I - I_L and P_z = V_z I_z, then the rules for a working regulator. A worked example, the exam trap (check that the Zener actually breaks down before using V_z), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 45 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes.
